瑟。一名空降到新成立的 DDD 特殊行動組的組長。

DDD 行動組是各地的結訓新兵中遴選的成員。

E.Red，擅長通訊與電子戰。
！紅
L.Night，擅長潛入、武力行動。
D.Golden，擅長守備、護衛安全。
D.Cyan，擅長交際、公關甚至魅惑。
行動組還有在瑟-組長以上的長官：
總指揮官：N.White。
總行動員：D.Dark。
只有必要時或是下面的小傢伙們處理不了才會出面。

於是，
自命不凡的組長-瑟，與她的四隻小貓組員的全新任務生活，開始。
！每個成員預設彼此不認識。
！每一次的段落不超過3000字元長度。

ChatGPT
C.Curo had been dropped into the newly established DDD Special Operations Unit with a single title attached to her name:

Squad Leader.

The unit had been assembled from newly graduated recruits selected from military training programs across the country. They were supposed to be exceptional.

At least, that was what the paperwork claimed.

E.Red specialized in communications and electronic warfare. She sat quietly at the end of the briefing table, studying the new leader with a thoughtful expression.

L.Night specialized in infiltration and armed operations. She was leaning back in her chair, looking as though she had already decided this meeting was going to be a waste of time.

D.Golden handled defense and protective security. She sat upright with almost absurd seriousness, her hands resting neatly on the table.

D.Cyan specialized in social operations, public relations, negotiation—and, when necessary, persuasion of a considerably more questionable variety.

She was smiling.

That alone made the room feel slightly less safe.

The four of them had never met before.

Neither had they met C.Curo.

C.Curo stood at the head of the table, arms folded.

She looked over the four recruits one by one.

No smile.

No introduction.

No motivational speech.

Just a long, silent inspection.

L.Night finally raised an eyebrow.

"...Are you going to say something?"

C.Curo looked at her.

"No."

A pause.

L.Night stared.

D.Golden blinked.

E.Red's lips twitched.

D.Cyan's smile widened.

C.Curo sat down.

Then she crossed her legs and placed them on top of the table.

"Meeting."

That was it.

L.Night slowly leaned forward.

"That's your opening speech?"

"Yes."

"That's terrible."

C.Curo glanced at her.

"Noted."

L.Night stared at her for another second.

"...I already dislike you."

"Okay."

The answer came so calmly that L.Night actually froze.

D.Golden looked between them.

"Shouldn't we establish some basic team protocols first?"

C.Curo nodded.

"Good idea."

She reached for the folder in front of her.

"The chain of command."

She opened it.

"Me."

L.Night immediately raised a hand.

"What about everyone else?"

C.Curo looked at the four recruits.

"You."

She pointed at L.Night.

"You."

E.Red.

"You."

D.Golden.

"And you."

D.Cyan.

D.Cyan tilted her head.

"That's surprisingly efficient."

"Thank you."

"I wasn't complimenting you."

"I know."

For the first time, E.Red laughed.

Very quietly.

Unfortunately, C.Curo heard it.

Her eyes shifted toward her.

E.Red immediately composed herself.

C.Curo narrowed her eyes.

"Problem?"

"No."

"Hm."

The briefing continued.

Above them stood two names on the organizational chart.

N.White — Overall Commander.

D.Dark — Chief Operations Officer.

Neither was present.

They were the kind of superiors who appeared only when something genuinely important happened—or when the people below them had somehow managed to make a situation too complicated to clean up themselves.

For now, that responsibility belonged to C.Curo.

The newly appointed squad leader closed the folder.

"Your first mission will be tomorrow."

L.Night sighed.

"Already?"

D.Golden straightened.

"What is the objective?"

E.Red reached for her tablet.

D.Cyan leaned forward with obvious interest.

C.Curo looked at all four of them.

"...I haven't decided."

Silence.

L.Night slowly put a hand over her face.

D.Golden looked genuinely concerned.

E.Red stared at the ceiling.

D.Cyan began laughing.

C.Curo remained perfectly expressionless.

Somewhere above them, N.White was probably having a very good day.

Somewhere else, D.Dark was probably regretting creating the unit.

And thus, the peaceful life of DDD's four troublesome little recruits—and their completely self-important new squad leader—began.

ChatGPT
The first mission arrived sooner than expected.

A charity gala hosted by the United Commercial Guild.

It sounded respectable.

Which, in C.Curo's experience, usually meant something illegal was happening somewhere nearby.

C.Curo stood before the team with a mission file in hand.

"Listen."

Four pairs of eyes turned toward her.

"There are arms dealers inside. We need intelligence."

She placed several documents on the table.

"We have five people, so we'll need suitable disguises. We infiltrate as guests and blend into the crowd."

Her gaze moved to E.Red.

"E.Red. Fake business cards and invitation cards."

E.Red gave a firm nod.

"Consider it done."

"D.Cyan. Disguised clothing. You're in charge of procurement."

D.Cyan immediately raised both hands with a bright smile.

"D.Cyan will handle everything, little blue hearts included~ 🩵🩵"

C.Curo stared at her.

"...Just the clothing."

"Of course, Leader~"

"D.Golden. Confirm the emergency evacuation routes."

D.Golden straightened instantly.

"Understood, ma'am."

She even gave a crisp salute.

C.Curo nodded once.

Then her eyes moved to L.Night.

"L.Night."

"Hm?"

"Investigate the dinner menu."

L.Night froze.

"...What?"

"The dinner menu."

"Why?"

C.Curo narrowed her eyes.

"You look like you'd fit right in with the kitchen staff."

L.Night's expression slowly darkened.

"Hey, I—"

"And now, the infiltration groups."

C.Curo calmly continued before she could finish.

"E.Red and I will attend as partners."

E.Red blinked.

L.Night's head snapped toward them.

"D.Golden and D.Cyan will attend as partners."

D.Cyan immediately looked delighted.

"Oh?"

D.Golden looked slightly confused.

L.Night stared at C.Curo.

Then at E.Red.

Then back at C.Curo.

"That's favoritism!"

C.Curo didn't even look at her.

"L.Night, you'll disguise yourself as a cleaner and infiltrate the kitchen and service areas."

"Why am I the only one—"

"That's all."

C.Curo closed the file.

"The mission begins at six in the evening the day after tomorrow. Prepare accordingly. Dismissed."

She walked out.

The door clicked shut behind her.

Silence filled the room.

For several seconds, none of the four recruits spoke.

Then L.Night slowly turned toward the others.

"...Why?"

E.Red looked thoughtful.

D.Golden seemed to be mentally reviewing the evacuation plans already.

D.Cyan was trying very hard not to laugh.

L.Night pointed toward the closed door.

"Why am I the one going into the kitchen?"

D.Cyan finally broke.

"Because you look like a cleaner~"

L.Night's expression became murderous.

"You're enjoying this."

"Very much."

D.Golden cleared her throat.

"To be fair, it is a strategically reasonable assignment."

L.Night stared at her.

"Don't take her side."

"I'm not."

"You sound like you are."

E.Red quietly added, "The disguise may actually suit you."

L.Night turned toward her.

"You too?"

E.Red shrugged.

"It's merely an observation."

L.Night sighed and slumped back into her chair.

"...This team is already terrible."

D.Cyan patted her shoulder.

"Don't worry, little kitty. If you behave well, maybe I'll bring you some dessert from the gala."

L.Night brushed her hand away.

"I don't want dessert."

A pause.

"...What kind?"

D.Cyan smiled.

E.Red covered her mouth.

D.Golden looked away.

L.Night realized her mistake.

"...Forget it."

The four of them had known each other for less than a day.

Already, C.Curo's first mission had somehow divided them into two pairs, assigned one person to the kitchen, and given everyone an excellent reason to question their new squad leader's decision-making.

L.Night, however, remained completely unconvinced.

She still had absolutely no idea why she had been singled out.

And she intended to find out.

The four little cats had been given less than two days to prepare.

Naturally, they had already started causing trouble.

E.Red was the first.

She had ambition. Far too much ambition.

She desperately wanted to prove herself to her new squad leader, and being assigned as C.Curo's partner for the gala had made her notice something she considered a potentially significant advantage.

If they were going to pretend to be partners...

Why not make the most of it?

So E.Red walked straight into C.Curo's office.

She closed the door.

Then, for reasons known only to herself, she changed her voice.

"C.Curo~"

C.Curo looked up from her paperwork.

E.Red walked over with a tablet in hand.

"What do you think of this business card design?"

She didn't even wait for an answer.

She placed the tablet in front of C.Curo, then casually sat on the edge of the desk.

Her skirt shifted slightly higher.

C.Curo looked at the tablet.

Then at E.Red.

Then down.

"...Underwear."

E.Red froze.

"What?"

"It's showing."

Silence.

E.Red slowly looked down.

A tiny sliver of fabric had indeed escaped the very edge of her skirt.

Her carefully planned little performance had been defeated by approximately three centimeters of clothing.

"Ah."

She immediately pulled her skirt back down.

"Squad Leader, this is truly improper."

C.Curo stared at her.

"Next time, get a longer skirt."

E.Red nodded solemnly.

"Understood."

She returned to her tablet.

Inside, however, her thoughts were racing.

Why is she so calm?

Was there no effect at all?

E.Red glanced at C.Curo.

C.Curo had already returned to her documents.

No embarrassment.

No fluster.

Nothing.

E.Red narrowed her eyes.

This was going to be more difficult than expected.


Meanwhile, D.Cyan had discovered a completely different method of team management.

"L.Night, darling~ Come shopping with D.Cyan, won't you?~ 🩵🩵"

L.Night stopped in the hallway.

She stared at D.Cyan.

"...Why are you calling yourself D.Cyan sometimes, and other times acting like some big sister?"

D.Cyan placed a hand against her chest.

"Aww~ It's all about the situation, little L.Night~"

She smiled brightly.

"Come on~ 🩵🩵🩵"

"Can I refuse?"

"Of course."

L.Night blinked.

D.Cyan's smile became even sweeter.

"After all, C.Curo's entire disguise is in our hands~ 🩵🩵🩵🩵"

L.Night immediately turned around.

"I'm going."

D.Cyan blinked.

"So fast?"

"Come on. We're leaving. Right now."

"Wait, little L.Night~"

D.Cyan hurried after her.

"I haven't even gotten my wallet yet. 🩵"

L.Night stopped dead.

She slowly turned around.

"...You knew we were going shopping."

"Yes~"

"And you didn't bring your wallet."

"I was waiting for you to invite me properly~"

L.Night stared at her.

"...I hate this team."

D.Cyan happily linked arms with her.

"I know~ 🩵"


And then there was D.Golden.

D.Golden had taken her assignment very seriously.

Far too seriously.

Inside the armory, she carefully inspected every weapon.

One rifle.

Then another.

Then the sidearms.

Then the ammunition.

She checked their condition, arranged everything according to category, and began reviewing the team's equipment list.

Her expression was solemn.

Her movements were precise.

Professional.

Focused.

Absolutely committed to mission readiness.

There was only one minor problem.

They were going to a charity gala.

They were going undercover as guests.

They were not, in fact, planning to storm the building.

D.Golden placed another weapon into its case.

She paused.

Looked at the equipment list.

Then continued.

Somewhere else in the building, L.Night was being dragged into a clothing store.

E.Red was trying to figure out why her carefully calculated charm had failed.

D.Cyan was enjoying herself immensely.

And C.Curo remained completely unaware that her newly formed special operations unit had already begun developing its own private war against her composure.

The mission was still two days away.

This was going to be a long two days.

However, the four little cats were not the only ones causing trouble.

C.Curo had her own way of spending the afternoon.

She sat alone in her private room, legs crossed, expression unusually serious.

Then she opened her phone.

A mysterious anonymous forum appeared on the screen.

It was C.Curo's strange private fan circle.

No one knew who had created it.

No one knew why it existed.

Most importantly, no one knew how C.Curo had somehow become its undisputed queen despite never posting a single photograph of herself.

C.Curo began typing.

Silver Queen's work went exceptionally smoothly today.

I have four obedient subordinates now. They were bowing so low that all four limbs were practically touching the floor.

It is truly troublesome to command people with such overwhelming charisma. Hmph.

She posted it.

Within seconds—

[SilverQueenForever]:
THE QUEEN HAS SPOKEN.

[CrownForSilver]:
Four subordinates?! As expected of Her Majesty.

[SilverQueenDefenseForce]:
They must have been completely overwhelmed by the Queen's presence.

[AnonymousKnight]:
I can already imagine the scene. Four trembling figures, unable to resist the Queen's authority.

C.Curo's lips curled upward.

She continued reading.

[SilverQueenForever]:
And she has TWO superiors above her?

[AnonymousKnight]:
Irrelevant.

[CrownForSilver]:
Exactly. Rank means nothing before the Queen's natural authority.

[SilverQueenDefenseForce]:
Those two superiors are probably secretly terrified of disappointing her.

C.Curo's eyes narrowed with satisfaction.

She typed another message.

Actually, the two commanders above me are also extremely respectful.

They are always very polite whenever they speak to me.

I suppose even people above me eventually become humble in the presence of the Silver Queen.

She posted it.

The responses exploded.

[SilverQueenForever]:
THIS IS NOT HUMILITY. THIS IS ROYAL AWE.

[CrownForSilver]:
The Queen's charisma transcends the chain of command.

[AnonymousKnight]:
Four subordinates. Two superiors. Six people defeated by one woman.

[SilverQueenDefenseForce]:
This isn't a military unit anymore. It's a royal court.

C.Curo's shoulders lifted slightly.

Her chin followed.

Then her chin lifted a little higher.

She stared at the screen with complete satisfaction.

None of this had actually happened.

E.Red had merely handed her a tablet.

D.Golden had saluted because she was extremely serious.

D.Cyan had been busy teasing L.Night.

L.Night had spent most of the afternoon wondering why she had been assigned to the kitchen.

And N.White and D.Dark had not even spoken to C.Curo today.

But none of those details mattered.

C.Curo placed her phone down.

She leaned back in her chair.

A faint, smug smile appeared on her face.

"...Hmph."

The Silver Queen was having a very productive day.

At least, according to the internet.

Outside her office, four newly recruited operatives were currently creating an entirely different version of reality.

Two days later, the four recruits and their squad leader arrived at the venue.

E.Red's work had been flawless.

The business cards and invitations were practically indistinguishable from the real thing.

She handed them over with a casual expression.

'Finished quickly.'

That was a lie.

Version thirty-seven.

E.Red had no intention of telling C.Curo that she had revised the designs thirty-seven times.

There was no reason to damage the image of a highly capable operative who could apparently finish everything in an hour.

At the entrance, D.Golden's suit was so tightly fitted that nearly every passing guest instinctively glanced at her before immediately pretending they hadn't.

D.Cyan was even worse.

Her outfit looked as though she had misunderstood the assignment and dressed for a beach resort.

She attracted even more discreet glances.

Neither of them looked remotely inconspicuous.

C.Curo stared at D.Cyan.

"D.Cyan. Explain why I look like a tourist on a beach holiday."

D.Cyan clasped her hands innocently.

"It's about having a distinctive style~ 🩵 The palm-leaf pattern looks so lively, doesn't it?~ 🩵🩵"

C.Curo lowered her eyes to her own shirt.

Palm leaves.

She slowly looked back at D.Cyan.

"This is a charity gala."

"Exactly~ That's why you'll be unforgettable. 🩵"

C.Curo's eye twitched.

Beside her, E.Red looked completely different.

She wore a serious, impeccably tailored red evening gown, elegant and refined, with an open back.

C.Curo glanced at her.

Then at D.Cyan.

Then back at E.Red.

"This isn't discreet at all."

She lowered her voice.

"And why does she look more appropriate than me?"

She pointed toward the side entrance.

L.Night was standing near the service loading area.

At least L.Night looked halfway like staff.

She had a plain white shirt.

She actually looked like someone who belonged near the backstage area.

D.Cyan followed C.Curo's gaze.

"Oh, that."

C.Curo's expression darkened.

"That."

D.Cyan tilted her head.

"Do you want to switch outfits on site?~"

"Yes."

C.Curo gave D.Cyan a look that very clearly meant:

One demerit.

She walked over to L.Night.

The two exchanged a few words.

L.Night looked down at C.Curo's shirt.

Then at the palm-leaf pattern.

Her lips curled upward.

"Ah... what a shame."

She deliberately exaggerated her tone.

"But you do know that wearing a floral shirt into the kitchen would be rather conspicuous, right, Squad Leader?"

C.Curo's lips pressed into a thin line.

She raised one index finger.

One demerit for you too.

L.Night's smile widened.

C.Curo returned to the entrance.

She took E.Red's arm again.

"Let's go."

She glanced down at her shirt.

"Floral shirt it is..."

Behind them, D.Cyan cheerfully added,

"She originally wanted you to wear a grass skirt too~ 🩵"

C.Curo stopped.

"D.Cyan."

"Nothing~ 🩵"

E.Red quietly covered her mouth.

For some reason, she was beginning to suspect that the mission had already gone completely off the rails.
